summary: Root cause identified with high confidence (0.80): portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905, deployed 2026-05-05T08:56Z by k.shah) introduced a new unindexed query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at against the shared ledger-db, executed as a sequential scan over ~48.2M rows on every call. That scan is the single slow-query signature in ledger-db's log over 08:45-11:00Z (360 occurrences, first at 08:58:38Z), and it accounts for the CPU step from ~30% to ~96%, the slow-query rate step from ~1/min to ~140/min, and ~190 held active connections all at the 08:58 minute. This contention starves order-service's INSERT INTO orders path, driving db_pool_in_use from ~14 to ~46 and p99 from ~150ms to ~5s with statement timeouts starting 09:00:42Z. The reported DBA autovacuum change (cfg-2903, 08:00Z) is a red herring: it produced no observable vacuum activity on trades/orders, and the storm post-dates it by ~58 minutes with no mechanical effect. order-service itself had no deployment or config change in the week.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service v4.5.0 unindexed trades query saturates shared ledger-db and starves order-service writes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The sole deployment in the window, portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905, 08:56Z), introduced a new unindexed query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at against the shared ledger-db. That query executes as a sequential scan over ~48.2M rows on each call, driving ledger-db CPU to ~96% and slow queries from ~1/min to ~140/min and holding ~190 active connections. This contention starves order-service's INSERT INTO orders path, pushing its db_pool_in_use from ~14 to ~46 and p99 from ~150ms to ~5s with statement timeouts. portfolio-service's own p99 also degrades, while low-volume read writers (payment/settlement) coast flat.

causal_chain.claim: portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905) deployed 08:56Z adding 'new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at', no migration/index
portfolio-service's only datastore is ledger-db, the same shared postgres order-service writes to
The new trades query runs as an unindexed Seq Scan over ~48.2M rows on every call
First slow-log occurrence of that query is 08:58:38Z, absent before 08:58; ledger-db CPU and slow-queries step at the 08:58 minute (after the 08:56 deploy)
~140/min Seq Scans saturate ledger-db CPU (~96%) and hold ~190 active connections near the ~200 cap
order-service's INSERT INTO orders path is starved: db_pool_in_use rises ~14->~46, statement timeouts, p99 ~5s
portfolio-service's own p99 degrades in the same step, consistent with its heavy workload hitting the saturated DB

assumptions: order-service is more sensitive than payment/settlement because its write path (INSERT) needs a connection/CPU slot that the long portfolio seq scans occupy; payment/settlement's low-volume reads were not starved (F28-F30)
The 08:45/08:52 coarse-bucket rise is an averaging artifact of the true 08:58 step (now supported by 1-min data F25/F26/F33)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Autovacuum change is a red herring; onset driven by the 08:56 deploy
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The reporter's autovacuum suspicion is a red herring; the observed onset maps precisely to the 08:56 portfolio-service deploy (CPU/slow-query step at 08:58, query slow-logs first at 08:58:38), and the sole slow-query signature is the new trades Seq Scan. This is now better expressed as H1; H5 is retained as the specific 'autovacuum ruled out' framing and largely folded into H1.

causal_chain.claim: Autovacuum change at 08:00 produced no visible effect and no vacuum activity (quiet gap + zero vacuum logs)
The only change aligned with the 08:58 step is the 08:56 portfolio deploy
Sole slow-query signature is the new unindexed trades Seq Scan over 48.2M rows
Shared-DB contention -> order-service pool saturation -> statement timeouts, p99 5s

ranked_hypotheses.title: DBA autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor change (0.2->0.1) triggered aggressive autovacuum that saturates ledger-db
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 08:00Z ledger-db config change (cfg-2903, scale_factor 0.2->0.1) caused frequent autovacuum runs on the shared instance, driving CPU and slow queries up and blocking order-service's INSERT INTO orders. This is the reporter's suspicion.

causal_chain.claim: autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor lowered 0.2->0.1 at 08:00Z, sole config change in the week
Aggressive autovacuum launches more frequent vacuum runs on shared ledger-db
Vacuum activity saturates ledger-db CPU and drives slow queries up
DB saturation blocks order-service INSERT INTO orders -> statement timeouts, p99 5s

assumptions: A scale_factor change actually produced measurable vacuum activity on the relevant tables (directly contradicted by F35)
The 08:58 step is attributable to a config change made 58 min earlier rather than the deploy 2 min earlier
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: F35 shows NO aggressive-vacuum activity: across 08:00-11:00 the only autovacuum log line is 'processed table public.audit_log' at the same ~8-15 min cadence as before, with no vacuum of trades/orders. F32 shows the slow queries begin only after the 08:56 deploy, not at the 08:00 change. F31 shows every slow query is the portfolio trades Seq Scan, not a vacuum. The 45-58 min quiet gap plus zero mechanical effect rules this out as the driver.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db infrastructure/resource failure (IOPS throttling or volume IO) independent of both changes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared ledger-db's underlying storage hit an IOPS/burst-credit or IO-throttling limit, throttling all queries and producing the CPU/slow-query/connection step change; order-service's timeouts are downstream. Same mechanism as HIST-110.

causal_chain.claim: Ledger-db underlying volume IOPS throttled (burst credits exhausted)
Throttled IO drives slow queries ~1/min -> ~140/min and CPU to ~96%
Throttled/contended DB blocks order-service writes -> statement timeouts and 5s p99

assumptions: A storage IOPS limit exists and was hit this time
The slow-query storm is coincidental with the deploy rather than caused by it
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The ~140/min slow-query storm is entirely accounted for by the portfolio trades Seq Scan signature that first appears 08:58:38 (F31/F32/F33/F34); a storage-throttling cause would slow existing queries indiscriminately but would not generate 360 copies of one specific new query. No IO metric exists to support throttling, and this is a precedent-only lead (F6/F24).

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service-side connection pool / dependency bottleneck; ledger-db timeouts are a symptom
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The bottleneck originates in order-service's own call path or pool configuration (db_pool or an upstream/downstream dependency such as pricing-engine, exchange-gateway or kafka), causing connections/pool to pile up and order writes to time out; ledger-db CPU rise is a consequence of blocked/retrying order-service connections rather than the cause.

causal_chain.claim: Something in order-service or its pool config throttles DB connection turnover
order-service db_pool_in_use rises ~14 -> ~46 and holds connections open
Held/blocked connections inflate ledger-db active connections to ~195
Statement timeouts on INSERT INTO orders and 5s p99

assumptions: No order-service release or config change occurred (F1/F14), so the origin would be a latent/runtime cause
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The DB CPU/slow-query storm is driven by the portfolio trades Seq Scan, not by order-service connections: the sole slow-query signature is portfolio-attributed (F31), and order-service's INSERTs never appear in the slow-query log (F36). order-service's pool rise is reactive to the slow DB, not causal. No order-service change exists (F1/F14).

facts.statement: The only deployment anywhere in the week 2026-04-28→2026-05-05T10:59Z is dep-5905, portfolio-service v4.5.0 at 2026-05-05T08:56:00Z by k.shah (status live, not rolled back), summarized as 'Add realised P&L breakdown to holdings API' with change 'new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at' and 'no migration included'; no order-service deployment or config change occurred.

The only config change in the window is cfg-2903: ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor changed 0.2→0.1 at 2026-05-05T08:00:00Z by dba-team; ledger-db is shared:true and is the db callee of four services (order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service).

Over 08:45-11:00Z ledger-db's slow-query log contains exactly one query signature: 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2 ORDER BY executed_at -- Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907) application_name=portfolio-service', appearing 360 times, with no other slow-query pattern.

The trades-query slow log first appears at 2026-05-05T08:58:38Z ('slow query 8690ms ... application_name=portfolio-service'); the signature is absent in ledger-db logs before 08:58, where the only preceding events are baseline 'checkpoint complete', 'autovacuum: processed table public.audit_log', and the 08:00:20Z config line.

The autovacuum change produced no observable aggressive-vacuum activity: across 08:00-11:00 the only autovacuum log line is 'autovacuum: processed table public.audit_log' at roughly the same ~8-15 min cadence as before the change, with no vacuum of the trades or orders tables.

At 1-minute resolution ledger-db CPU is flat ~28-32% through 08:57 then steps to 95.62% at 08:58 and 96.36% at 08:59; slow_queries_per_min is ~1.4/min at 08:56 then jumps to 139.43 avg (max 139.68) at 08:58, sustained ~137-142/min through 10:58.

ledger-db active connections rise from a stable ~54-68 (05:00-08:30) to ~189-195 avg (max 200.5-212.35) from 09:00 onward, roughly 3x baseline and near a ~200-connection level, while disk_used_pct stays flat at ~70.8-71.4% across the whole 05:00-10:45 window.

order-service p99 latency steps from a flat ~145-165ms through the 08:56 bucket to 2878ms avg (max 5607.8ms) in the 08:58 bucket, sustained ~5000-5600ms from 09:00 through 10:52; order-service db_pool_in_use rises from a flat ~13.8-14.2 to ~44-47 sustained from 09:04 to 10:56.

order-service errors are a single signature: 284 ERROR lines 'ledger-db: canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders) orderId=<n>', first_seen 2026-05-05T09:00:42Z, still occurring at 10:58:29Z; no other error pattern appears.
No 'INSERT INTO orders' or order-service-attributed slow query appears in ledger-db's own slow-query log; the pattern list is entirely the portfolio trades query.

The two other shared ledger-db writers did not degrade: payment-service p99 stays ~309-327ms and settlement-service p99 ~235-249ms with no step at 08:45-09:00, and their db_pool_in_use stays flat (payment ~7.7-8.5, settlement ~5.8-6.4) — unlike order-service's pool which stepped to ~44-47.

portfolio-service p99 latency steps from a flat ~175-187ms through the 08:44 bucket to 1878.12ms avg (max 7056.7) in the 08:52 bucket and ~6700-7130ms sustained from 09:00 onward; the 08:52 bucket covers 08:52-09:00 and contains the 08:56 deploy.

The 08:00Z autovacuum change strictly precedes onset but with a 45-58 min gap (45 min before the 08:45 CPU bucket, 56-58 min before the order-service p99 step), whereas the 08:56 deploy sits inside the same 08:56-08:58 bucket as the p99 step.

portfolio-service's only datastore is ledger-db (db edge portfolio-service→ledger-db), the same shared postgres order-service writes to; order-service's own path is api-gateway → order-service → {ledger-db, pricing-engine, exchange-gateway, kafka}.

Historical precedent: HIST-111 (2025-05-22) is the same pattern — 'New report query without index did sequential scans' on ledger-db — while HIST-110 (2026-01-15) matched symptoms but was caused by IOPS throttling; no indexed historical incident was caused by an autovacuum parameter change.

assumptions: Assumption: order-service is more sensitive than payment/settlement because its write path (INSERT) needs a connection/CPU slot that the long portfolio Seq Scans occupy, whereas payment/settlement's low-volume reads were not starved (their flat latency/pool metrics F28-F30).

Assumption: the 08:45/08:52 coarse-bucket rise in CPU/slow-query/connection metrics is an averaging artifact of the true 08:58 step, since the 1-minute-resolution data (F25/F26/F33) shows flat baseline through 08:57.

Assumption: the link from the unindexed trades Seq Scan to CPU/connection saturation is inferred from the query-plan signature (Seq Scan over 48.2M rows, 0.9-8.8s per execution) plus the coincident one-minute metric step, not from pg_stat_statements or EXPLAIN attribution, which were unavailable.
Assumption: the trades table lacks a suitable index for the (account_id, executed_at) filter, inferred from the observed Seq Scan plan; no direct index listing was retrieved.
Assumption: no other hidden deployment or config change outside the queried systems contributed to the onset; established only for the systems reachable via the change/deployment tools.

Assumption: rollback status of dep-5905 (rolled_back_at null at data pull) reflects the state at investigation time and no post-hoc mitigation was applied by another actor whose actions were outside the queried systems.

timeline.event: DBA change cfg-2903 applied to shared ledger-db: autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2→0.1 ('More aggressive autovacuum'). Produces no observable vacuum activity on trades/orders afterwards.
Deployment dep-5905: portfolio-service v4.5.0 by k.shah goes live, adding a new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at with no migration — the only deployment in the week.
ledger-db 1-minute metrics step: CPU 32%→95.6%, slow_queries_per_min 1.4→139.4; first trades Seq Scan slow log at 08:58:38Z (8690ms).
order-service p99 steps from ~150ms to 2878ms avg (max 5607.8ms) in the 08:58 bucket; db_pool_in_use rises toward ~44-47.
portfolio-service p99 begins stepping upward (1878ms avg, max 7056.7ms) in the 08:52 bucket that contains the 08:56 deploy; sustained ~6.7-7.1s from 09:00.
ledger-db active connections reach ~189-195 avg (max 212.35), ~3x the ~54-68 baseline; order-service db_pool_in_use sustained ~44-47.
First order-service error: 'ledger-db: canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders) orderId=<n>'.
Incident INC-009 [SEV-1] reported: order-service p99 > 5s with statement timeouts against ledger-db; reporter suspects the morning autovacuum change.
order-service statement-timeout errors on INSERT INTO orders still occurring; ledger-db CPU ~96.5% and slow queries ~140/min persist through the end of available data (10:58).

recommended_actions.action: Roll back portfolio-service from v4.5.0 to the last version, or disable the new 'realised P&L breakdown' holdings API endpoint that issues the account_id + executed_at trades query (dep-5905, deployed 08:56Z) — e.g. feature-flag/route-disable the endpoint or revert the deploy.
recommended_actions.rationale: That deploy is the sole change on ledger-db's dependency path at the 08:58 onset and its query is the only slow-query signature in the DB log; removing it should immediately relieve the Seq Scans driving CPU ~96%, ~140 slow queries/min and ~190 held connections, restoring order-service's INSERT throughput. Evidence: F1, F5, F17, F31, F32, F33, F25, F26.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back or further tune the ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor setting (cfg-2903) as an incident response; leave it at 0.1 unless the DBA team has independent reasons.
recommended_actions.rationale: The change produced no observable vacuum activity on trades/orders and the storm post-dates it by ~58 minutes with no mechanical effect, so reverting it will not mitigate and would conflate the change record. Evidence: F2, F35, F32, F15.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm mitigation by re-checking, after the rollback, ledger-db cpu_pct and slow_queries_per_min returning toward ~30% and ~1/min, active connections falling back toward ~54-68, and order-service p99 returning toward ~150ms with zero new 'canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)' errors.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the exact baseline-vs-incident metrics that characterized the fault; verifying the inverse step confirms H1 and rules out coincidental recovery. Evidence: F8, F9, F10, F11, F12, F25, F26, F33.

recommended_actions.action: Add a supporting index for the new query (e.g. on trades(account_id, executed_at)) or rewrite it so it does not sequentially scan the ~48.2M-row trades table, then verify with EXPLAIN that the plan no longer shows 'Seq Scan on trades' and that per-execution time drops from hundreds of ms-8.8s.
recommended_actions.rationale: The query plan evidence shows every execution full-scans ~48.2M rows with no index used; an index is the durable fix for the query itself. Evidence: F31, F34, F5.

recommended_actions.action: Add connection-pool / query timeout isolation for order-service's write path against the shared ledger-db (e.g. separate pool or per-service resource guarantees) so one client's long scans cannot exhaust ~200 connections and starve order writes.
recommended_actions.rationale: order-service's pool saturates reactively (~14→~46) as ledger-db connections are held near ~200 by long portfolio scans, while payment/settlement stayed flat — showing cross-tenant contention on a shared DB. Evidence: F3, F12, F13, F16, F30, F36.

recommended_actions.action: Require index/EXPLAIN review for new queries against the shared ledger-db as a pre-merge/pre-deploy gate, and add alerting on ledger-db slow_queries_per_min and CPU step changes.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the second time an unindexed report query caused sequential scans on ledger-db (HIST-111), and the ~140x slow-query step was detectable in minutes; a review gate and a slow-query/cpu alert would catch it pre-production and reduce MTTR. Evidence: F6, F19, F24, F11, F26, F33.

recommended_actions.action: After mitigation, verify that the shared ledger-db's other writers (payment-service, settlement-service, portfolio-service) show no residual error signatures by pulling their error_rate and logs, since this was never queried during the incident.
recommended_actions.rationale: Flat latency/pool metrics for payment/settlement (F28-F30) support the selective-starvation mechanism but their error streams and portfolio-service's pool state were unverified; confirming them closes the blast-radius picture and guards against a recurrence going unnoticed.

data_gaps: No pg_stat_statements view, per-query call counts, or rows_read/seq_scan counters exist for ledger-db (available_metrics are only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min), so attribution of CPU and connections rests on the slow-query log signature plus the coincident metric step rather than on query-level cumulative statistics.

No per-table autovacuum/vacuum-run, xid-age or effective per-table parameter data was retrievable (no metric-query tool for postgres internals), so the 08:00Z scale_factor change could not be mechanically validated or falsified — though the absence of trades/orders vacuum log lines argues it had no effect.

No IO, lock, checkpoint or storage-burst metric exists for ledger-db, so DB-internal contention mechanisms (locks, buffer cache, checkpoint storms) and the HIST-110 IOPS-throttling precedent could not be fully excluded by direct measurement; disk_used_pct is the only storage-related signal and was flat.

payment-service, settlement-service and portfolio-service error_rate and log data were not retrieved (tool budget exhausted), so whether they produced statement-timeout/error signatures (despite flat latency) and whether portfolio-service's own pool saturated remain unverified — blast radius is established only for order-service's write path.

No EXPLAIN output and no index listing for the trades table were obtained; the 'unindexed' claim rests on the observed 'Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)' plan in the slow-query log rather than an index catalog check.

Onset ordering is limited by metric bucket resolution (8-min buckets on 24h views, 2-min on zoomed views); the ledger-db CPU step is bracketed to 08:45-09:00 on coarse data and pinned to the 08:58 minute only in the 1-minute-resolution view.
Rollback status of dep-5905 and cfg-2903 was only read at data-pull time (rolled_back_at null); any post-hoc mitigation by another actor outside the queried systems is not reflected.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: The same ~140/min slow-query storm and ledger-db CPU step persisting unchanged after a full rollback/disable of portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905) would falsify H1 and re-open H2/H3.
Discovery of a hidden deployment or config change on a ledger-db client (or on ledger-db itself) just before 08:58Z would provide a competing onset driver.
Direct autovacuum evidence (per-table vacuum runs or xid-age statistics showing aggressive vacuum on trades/orders starting near 08:58) would revive H2 as the driver.
Evidence of storage IOPS/burst-credit throttling at 08:58Z (an IO metric or throttling log line) would revive H3 and the HIST-110 precedent.

Evidence that order-service's slowness originated in its own call path or a dependency other than ledger-db (e.g. pricing-engine/exchange-gateway/kafka saturation) with ledger-db timeouts merely symptomatic would revive H4.

An index catalog check showing the trades(account_id, executed_at) query is in fact indexed — contradicting the observed Seq Scan plan — would undercut the mechanism linking the new query to DB saturation.

findings.statement: No deployment of order-service occurred in the window 2026-05-04→2026-05-05T10:59Z. Across all services the only deployment was portfolio-service v4.5.0 at 2026-05-05T08:56:00Z by k.shah (status live, not rolled back), whose summary is 'Add realised P&L breakdown to holdings API' with change 'new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at' and 'no migration included'.

Exactly one config change exists in the window: ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor changed from 0.2 to 0.1 at 2026-05-05T08:00:00Z by dba-team, described as 'More aggressive autovacuum'. No other service had a config change, and the change is on ledger-db (a shared platform-owned postgres), not on order-service.

ledger-db is marked shared:true and is the callee of db edges from FOUR services — order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service — so all four share the same ledger-db component that the autovacuum change touched.

order-service's dependency path is: api-gateway → order-service → {ledger-db (db), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway (http), kafka (queue-produce)}; pricing-engine in turn calls market-data-service and redis-cache. Other shared components on the path are redis-cache (shared:true, used by pricing-engine and portfolio-service) and kafka (shared:true).

The portfolio-service v4.5.0 deploy (08:56) writes to ledger-db via a 'new query on trades filtered by account_id + executed_at' with no migration — i.e. the neighbor deploy immediately preceding the 09:10 report issues a new, presumably unindexed query against the same shared database order-service uses.

findings.statement: Precedent lead only: HIST-110 (2026-01-15) had the identical symptom set — order-service + ledger-db, 'order latency','statement timeouts','slow queries' — but its recorded root cause was 'Cloud volume burst credits exhausted; IOPS throttled', fixed by moving to provisioned IOPS, not by autovacuum. HIST-111 (2025-05-22) shows a related pattern on the same DB: an unindexed new report query caused sequential scans and slowed ledger-db. No historical incident in the index was caused by an autovacuum parameter change.

Which of the two (or neither) drove the onset cannot be settled from change data alone.

findings.statement: Blast-radius / dependency map confirms the portfolio deploy lands on order-service's own dependency: portfolio-service's only datastore is ledger-db ('from':'portfolio-service','to':'ledger-db','kind':'db'), the same shared postgres that order-service writes to; portfolio-service also reaches a second shared component, redis-cache (shared:true). So both candidate changes act on order-service's dependency path, while order-service itself only calls ledger-db, pricing-engine, exchange-gateway and kafka.

Precedent leads only (not evidence about this incident): HIST-111 (2025-05-22) is exactly the competing-change pattern — services ['ledger-db','settlement-service'], symptoms ['slow queries','high db cpu'], root_cause 'New report query without index did sequential scans', match_score 3, the highest score returned. HIST-110 (2026-01-15) matches the current symptom set (order latency, statement timeouts, slow queries) but its cause was IOPS throttling. A targeted search for autovacuum-caused latency at shared databases returned no matching incident: the top results were HIST-101/HIST-107/HIST-109/HIST-110, none autovacuum-related.

findings.statement: T6 could not be completed as specified: my available toolset in this round contains no metric-query capability (only deployments, config changes, dependency graph, and historical-incident search), so I could not retrieve vacuum runs, per-table vacuum/xid-age statistics, or effective per-table autovacuum parameters for ledger-db. These are metric-class queries that none of my tools expose.

Re-confirmed independently (T6): in the window 2026-05-05T07:00→10:59Z there is exactly ONE config change on ledger-db — cfg-2903, key autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor, old_value 0.2 → new_value 0.1, changed_at 2026-05-05T08:00:00Z, author dba-team, description 'More aggressive autovacuum'. No other postgres parameter changed alongside scale_factor in that window.

Widening the config-change window to the full week 2026-04-28→2026-05-05T10:59Z across ALL services still returns exactly one change (cfg-2903 ledger-db autovacuum scale_factor). So no second postgres/autovacuum-adjacent parameter change occurred anywhere, confirming the 08:00 scale_factor change is the sole DB-side config event.

ledger-db has no deployment of its own (count 0 in window 07:00-10:59Z) and is a shared:true postgres owned by 'platform'; the only deployment anywhere in the 08:00-10:59Z window is dep-5905 portfolio-service v4.5.0 at 08:56Z. A config-only change on a shared managed DB is therefore the only DB-side mechanism attributable to the DBA action.

Precedent check (lead only): search for autovacuum-caused latency at shared databases returned no autovacuum-attributed incident; the top hits were HIST-101 (bcrypt cost), HIST-107 (cache storm), HIST-110 (IOPS throttling on order-service+ledger-db), HIST-113 (pricing-engine CPU). This is consistent with the team's F6/F19 but is NOT evidence that autovacuum did or did not run here.

ledger-db CPU at 1-minute resolution is flat ~28-32% through 08:57, then steps to 95.62% at 08:58, 96.36% at 08:59, 94.07% at 09:00. So the DB CPU step begins in the 08:58 minute, not the 08:45-08:56 buckets — the step precedes/interleaves the 08:56 portfolio deploy by ~2 min.

ledger-db slow_queries_per_min at 1-minute/2-min resolution is flat ~0.6-1.4/min through 08:56 (08:56 avg 1.43, max 1.52), then jumps to 139.43 avg (max 139.68) at 08:58 — same 08:58 step as CPU. Baseline from 08:30 is ~1/min.

portfolio-service (the service deployed at 08:56) p99 latency is flat ~175-187ms from 05:00 through the 08:44 bucket, then steps to 1878.12 avg (max 7056.7) in the 08:52 bucket and ~6700-7130ms sustained from 09:00 onward. Its onset bucket (08:52) is EARLIER than the ledger-db CPU/slow-query 08:58 step, but the 08:52 bucket covers 08:52-09:00 and contains the 08:56 deploy.

payment-service p99 latency is flat across the whole window with NO step at 08:45-09:00: ~309-327ms throughout, including 08:44 avg 321.83, 08:52 avg 315.04, 09:00 avg 313.94, 10:52 avg 325.69. The other shared ledger-db writer shows no degradation.

settlement-service p99 latency is also flat across the window with no step: ~235-249ms throughout, including 08:44 avg 237.87, 08:52 avg 245.0, 09:00 avg 242.59, 10:52 avg 238.89. The second shared ledger-db writer shows no degradation.

payment-service and settlement-service db_pool_in_use are flat across 08:00-10:56 (payment ~7.7-8.5, e.g. 08:52 avg 8.0, 09:00 avg 8.01; settlement ~5.8-6.4, e.g. 08:52 avg 6.01, 09:00 avg 6.03), with no rise at 08:45-09:00 — unlike order-service's pool which stepped to ~44-47 (F13). So their DB pools were not saturated despite the shared DB's CPU/slow-query step.

Over 08:45-11:00Z, ledger-db's slow-query log contains exactly ONE query signature: 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2 ORDER BY executed_at -- Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907) application_name=portfolio-service', appearing 360 times as WARN entries (no other slow-query pattern in the result). This is literally the new portfolio-service v4.5.0 query, executed as a sequential scan over ~48.2M rows.

findings.statement: First occurrence of the trades-query slow log is 2026-05-05T08:58:38Z ('slow query 8690ms: SELECT * FROM trades ... application_name=portfolio-service'). A scan of ledger-db logs back to 06:00Z shows this signature absent before 08:58 and the only preceding events being baseline 'checkpoint complete' and 'autovacuum: processed table public.audit_log' plus the 08:00:20Z config line — so the trades-query slow logs begin only after the 08:56 portfolio deploy, not at the 08:00 autovacuum change.

findings.statement: The ledger-db slow_queries_per_min metric steps from baseline to the reported level in the same bucket as the trades query's first appearance: 0.92 (08:40), 0.87 (08:46), 1.21 (08:52) — all ~1/min baseline — then 142.11 avg / 148.81 max in the 08:58 bucket, sustained ~137-142/min through 10:58 (last 140.71). So the ~140/min slow-query rate the task asks about is composed of this trades query.

Every slow-query log line names the offending access path as a Seq Scan over a ~48.2M-row trades table with no index used, and each single execution takes hundreds of ms to ~8.8s (e.g. 8690ms, 8823ms, 8555ms, 964ms). This is the query-plan evidence the task asked for: the trades query is unindexed and full-scans the whole table on each call, which plausibly saturates CPU (~96%) and holds connections (~190 active, near the ~200 cap).

findings.statement: The autovacuum change (cfg-2903 at 08:00:20Z, autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor=0.1) produced NO observable aggressive-vacuum activity: across 08:00-11:00 the only autovacuum log line is 'autovacuum: processed table public.audit_log' (13 occurrences, roughly one every ~8-15 min, same cadence as before the change), with no vacuum of the trades or orders tables and no autovacuum-attributable CPU/latency signature. This argues against H2 as the driver.

No 'INSERT INTO orders' or order-service-attributed slow query appears in ledger-db's own slow-query logs (the pattern list is entirely the portfolio trades query), while ledger-db active connections rise from ~62 (08:00-08:30) to 189-195 avg from 09:00 (max 212.35) — consistent with many long portfolio Seq Scans occupying the connection slots and starving order-service's INSERTs of CPU/IO. The failing statement timeout is seen on the order-service side, not as a ledger-db slow-log entry.
